Charts span 2 cols, actions panel 1. Transactions span 2, feed 1. */ ``` - Gap between cards: 16px. Page padding: 16–24px. - KPI tiles (balance, utilization, rewards, alerts) are small glass cards in a row. - Keep generous breathing room inside each card — labels at top, big number below, chart/meta at bottom. --- ## Step 5 — The Iridescent Payment Card (signature element) The hero of the dashboard is a credit/debit card with a holographic, iridescent finish. On: track filled with `--accent-grad`, with a soft `--accent-glow` shadow. White knob. ### Actions Panel A vertical list of row items (Freeze, Set limits, Reveal details, Replace card) each with a leading line icon, label, and a trailing chevron or toggle. One row may be disabled (`--text-3`, reduced opacity) like "Request increase". ### Upgrade / Promo Tile A small glass card lit with the full `--accent-grad` glow — a gradient background wash plus a sparkle icon. Copy like "Upgrade to Platinum". This is the one tile allowed to use the gradient as a fill. ### Transactions Table Columns: checkbox · ID/merchant · amount (tabular nums, right-aligned) · status chip · date · expand chevron. Header row in `--text-3`. Row dividers are 1px `--glass-border`. Row hover lifts to `--glass-2`. Thin line icons (1.5px stroke), `--text-2` default, `--text-1` on hover. Never use emojis as icons anywhere in the UI (no emoji in nav, buttons, status rows, feed items, or chips) — every icon must be a proper SVG from an icon library. Status chips use a small colored dot or a library icon, never an emoji. --- ## Step 7 — Data Visualization Charts glow. They sit inside glass cards on the dark background. ### Area / Line Chart (primary) - Line: 2px, stroked with `--accent-grad` (use a gradient stroke or `--accent-2`). - Glow: apply a soft drop-shadow filter to the line so it appears lit: `filter: drop-shadow(0 0 6px var(--accent-glow))`. - Fill: a vertical gradient from `rgba(accent, 0.18)` at the line down to transparent. - A horizontal dashed reference line (e.g. "Budget limit", "Risk limit", "Safe zone") in `--text-3`. - Tooltip: a small glass chip with the value and label, glowing dot on the data point. ### Ring / Donut (portfolio allocation) - Track: `--glass-2`. Segments: distinct accent-family hues. Center holds a big number + label. - Legend rows with a colored dot, label, and percentage (tabular nums). ### Bar / Sparkline - Bars: `--accent-grad` vertical fill, rounded tops, 6–10px wide. Inactive/comparison bars in `--glass-3`. ### Chart.js / library globals - Grid lines: `rgba(255,255,255,0.05)`. Axis text: `--text-3`, 11px. - No chart borders or boxes — the glass card is the container. - Always show tabular-num values; format currency in tooltips. --- ## Step 8 — Micro-Animations Keep motion subtle and premium. Nothing bouncy. - **Card hover:** background `--glass-1 → --glass-2`, border brightens, 200ms ease. - **Payment card sheen:** the slow diagonal light sweep (Step 5), 6s loop. - **Number count-up:** KPI numbers count from 0 to value on first load, ~600ms ease-out. - **Chart line draw-in:** stroke-dashoffset animation, ~800ms ease, on mount. - **Toggle:** knob slides 200ms; the gradient glow fades in when switched on. - **Chart tooltip:** fades + slides 6px into place, 150ms. - **Promo tile:** very slow gradient shift (background-position) for a living shimmer. - Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` — disable sheen, count-up, and shimmer; keep static states. --- ## Step 9 — Dark Mode Contrast Rules Glass on dark can fail readability fast. Enforce these: - Primary numbers use `--text-1` (95% white) — never dim the hero metric. - Never put `--text-3` (40%) text on the lightest glass; reserve it for the darker base background. - Status chips must keep their colored text at full saturation — don't lower chip text opacity. - The payment card's masked number and labels need a real contrast floor; if the iridescent fill is bright behind them, add a subtle dark gradient scrim behind the text. - Maintain at least a visible 1px border on every glass surface — without it, cards disappear into the background. --- ## Step 10 — Anti-Patterns (Never Do These) - Never: Solid opaque cards. Surfaces must be translucent glass with backdrop blur. - Never: Pure black `#000000` background. Use the deep blue-black `--bg-page`. - Never: Bright solid-color card fills (lime, purple blocks). The color lives in glows and the iridescent card, not in flat fills. - Never: The neon gradient everywhere. It's an accent glow — hero card, primary chart, one promo tile, active toggles. Not on every element. - Never: Hard drop shadows. Elevation comes from blur, border, and soft accent glow. - Never: Sharp corners. Everything is rounded (20px cards, 999px pills). - Never: Inconsistent status colors. Green = done, amber = pending, rose = failed. Never reuse them decoratively. - Never: Non-tabular numbers in tables. Always `tabular-nums`. - Never: Emojis as icons. Use real SVG icons from a library (Lucide, Heroicons, Phosphor) everywhere. --- ## Step 11 — Output Rules - Build the full dashboard, not fragments: top bar (search + range toggle) → hero payment card + KPI tiles → chart + actions panel → transactions table + activity feed → footer/promo row. - Use realistic financial data — real merchant names, plausible amounts, varied statuses. - Single self-contained file when possible; inline the CSS variables from Step 2 at the top. - Default to desktop dashboard layout unless the user asked for mobile. - Every surface is a glass card. Every number is formatted. Every status is a chip. The iridescent card anchors the screen. ENDOFFILE)
